METHODS OF CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF BRONZES
PART 2 DETERMINATION OF MANGANESE METHOD PHOTOMETRIC

( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD
( Part 2 ) (First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 22 July 1987, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis of Non-Ferrous Metals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 IS : 4027 first published in 1967, covered determination of copper aluminium, lead, tin, manganese, phosphorus, nickel, iron, silicon, zinc and antimony in bronzes. While reviewing this standard, the Sectional Committee decided that it is convenient to revise this standard in series of parts which, on publication, supersede the relevant method for determination given in IS : 4027-1967*. This part is one of that by photometric series and covers the determination of manganese method. The other parts are as follows: Part Part Part Part Part 1 3 4 5 6 Determination Determination Determination Determination Determination of of of of of copper and lead by electrolytic method phosphorus by volumetric method nickel by photometric method tin by iodimetric method zinc by complexometric (EDTA) method

0.1 This Indian Standard

Methods for chemical analysis of other constituents in bronzes, namely, aluminium, iron, silicon and antimony are under preparation and will be published iq subsequent parts of above series. 0.3 The method for determination `of manganese by the bismuthatevolumetric method stipulated in earlier edition has been substituted by periodate-photometric method. 0.4 The methods of analysis prescribed in this standard may primarily serve as referee methods and may also be used by the laboratories for their day-to-day work. Due consideration has been given in the preparation of this standard to the facilities available in the country for such analysis. *Methods of Chemical analysis of bronzes. 3

0.5 In reportin,g the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, the final value, observed or calculated, shall be rounded ofl in accordance with IS :`2 - 1960*.

1.1 This standard ( Part 2 ) prescribes a method for determination manganese in the range as specified in the relavent Indian Standards bronzes. 2. SAMPLING 2.1 Samples shall be drawn and prepared in accordance 1961t. 3. QUALITY OF REAGENTS

with IS : 1817 -

3.1 Unless specified otherwise, analytical grade reagents and distilled water ( see IS : 1070 - 1977$ ) shall be employed in this test. 4. DETERMINATION PHOTOMETRIC OF MANGANESE METHOD BY THE PERIODATE -

4.1 Outline of the Method - Manganese in an acid solution is oxidized to permanganate with potassium periodate. Photometric measurement is made at 520 nm. concentration range is 4.2 Concentration Range - The recommended from 0'1 to 2 mg of manganese in 100 ml of solution, using a cell depth of 1'000 cm. 4.3 Reagents 4.3.1 Hydrofluoric - Boric Acid Mixture - Add 200 ml of hydroff uoric acid to 1 800 ml of a saturated solution of boric acid. and mix. The mixture may be stored in a glass bottle.

Cool, make up to 1 litre in a volumetric flask and mix. 4.4 Procedure 4.4.1 Transfer two 0'500 g portions of a sample in the form of fine drillings or sawings to 300-ml Erlenmeyer flasks. 4.4.2 Add 15 ml of hydrofluoric-boric acid mixture, 15 ml of dilute nitric acid and 5 ml of phosphoric acid. 15 ml of water,

4.4.3 Allow dissolution to proceed without applying heat until reaction has nearly ceased. Heat to SO to 90�C until brown fumes have been expelled. 4.4.4 Add to first portion approximately 0'3 g of potassium periodate. Heat to boiling, boil gently for 2 minutes and then digest just below the Cool boiling point for 20 minutes to develop full intensity of colour. to room temperature, make up to loo-ml in a volumetric flask and mix. 4.4.5 Treat the second portion as in 4.4.4 without adding periodate. 4.4.6 Measure the absorbance of the first portion ( after 4.4.4 ) against the second portion ( after 4.4.5 ) at 520 nm. 4.4.7 Compute the manganese content from a calibration 4.5 Calibration Curve 4.5.1 Transfer 0'500 g of manganese free copper into each of seven 300-ml erlenmeyer flasks and add 0, 1'0, 3'0, 5'0, 10'0, 15'0 and 20 ml of manganese solution ( 1 ml = 0'1 mg of Mn ). 4.5.2 Proceed as in 4.4.2 to 4.4.4. 4.5.3 Measure absorbances of standards against reagent blank. 4.5.4 Plot absorbance values against mg of manganese per 100 ml of solution. 4.6 Calculation Manganese, where A = mg of manganese found in 100 ml of the final solution, and B = g of sample represented 5 in 100 ml of the final solution. percent = $ X &curve.
